title: Probability of matching a circuit at one input
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $C$ be a directed acyclic circuit with $n$ Boolean inputs, gates ordered so each gate reads only earlier vertices, and a valid output vertex, and let $x$ be an input. If a Boolean function on these inputs is chosen uniformly at random, the probability that its value at $x$ equals the value computed by $C$ at $x$ is $1/2$.
hypotheses_covered: The gates are ordered so each gate reads only earlier vertices
The output is a circuit vertex
$x$ is a Boolean input on the $n$ coordinates
